full_judgment:
Md. Nuruzzaman J.: This Civil Appeal, by leave, has arisen out of the judgment and order dated 15.03.2010 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.841 of 1999 making the Rule absolute and thereby setting aside the judgment and decree dated 04.01.1999 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong in Other Appeal No.122 of 1997 reversing those dated 27.02.1997 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, 2nd Additional Court at Sadar, Chittagong in Other Suit No.61 of 1990. 

 4. The defendant Nos.3 and 4 contended that the defendant No.1 proposed to sell the suit land, made an agreement with these defendants on 02.12.1974 receiving Tk.10,000/- out of total consideration of Tk.25,000/- and delivered possession. The defendant No.1 denied to execute and register the sale deed. Accordingly, these defendants filed Title Suit No.23 of 1977 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong and got a compromise decree. These defendants had no knowledge about the "bainanama" of the plaintiff. 

 5. The plaintiff by amending the plaint sought for declaration that the kabala deed executed by the defendant No. 1 in favour of the defendant Nos.3-4 pursuant to the decree passed in Other Suit No.23 of 1977, are void, collusive, ineffective and the same is not binding upon the plaintiff. He further prayed for declaration that the decree obtained by the defendant Nos.3 and 4 in Other Class Suit No.23 of 1977 is also void and the same is not binding upon the plaintiff. 

 6. On conclusion of the trial, the learned Assistant Judge, 2nd Additional Court at Sadar, Chittagong considering the evidences and documents on record decreed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 27.02.1997. 

 7. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the defendant Nos.3-4 as appellant preferred Other Appeal No.122 of 1997 before the learned District Judge, Chittagong. On transfer, the said appeal was heard by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong who by his judgment and decree dated 04.01.1999 allowed the appeal and there-by set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. 

 8. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgment and decree dated 04.01.1999 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong, the plaintiff preferred Civil Revision No.841 of 1999 before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule. 

 9. In due course, a Single Bench of the High Court Division upon hearing the par-ties made the Rule absolute by the impugned judgment and order dated 15.03.2010 and thereby set aside the judgment and decree dated 04.01.1999 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong in Title Appeal No.122 of 1997 and thereby affirmed the judgment and decree dated 27.02.1997 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 2nd Additional Court at Sadar, Chittagong in Other Suit No.61 of 1990. 

 11. Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that having regard to the admitted fact that the land described in the "bainanama" of the plaintiff and that of the decree these defendant appellants are not the same lands and having further regard to the fact that the High Court Division came to the finding that the suit land of Other Suit No. 61 of 1990/54 of 1976  are not identical with the suit land in Other Suit No.23 of 1977 and there is no clash of interest between the defendant Nos.3-4 and the plaintiff with respect to the agreement as Ext.4-bainanama, but the High Court Division committed an error of law in set-ting aside the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court. He further submits that the High Court Division has committed an error of law in not holding that the plaintiff, by filing Other Suit No. 61 of 1990/54 of 1976 for specific performance of contract, has not acquired any legal right in the suit land and hence, he is not entitled to get declaration that the judgment and decree passed in another suit between different parties being Other Suit No.23 of 1977 in respect of the different suit land as illegal and void and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. Hence, the instant appeal may kindly be allowed. However, he finally concedes that he has no submission against the decree of the suit land so far it relates to a decree of specific performance of contract. 

 12. Per contra, Mr. Mostafa Newaz Mohammad, the learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent No.1 made submissions in supports of the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. He submits that the plaintiff proved the fact of a valid contract, due execution of agreement by Shishu Bala and payment of earnest money and the suit was instituted within time, and the defendants failed to discard or contradict those facts. Hence, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute and legally restored the judgment and decree of the trial Court by setting aside the judgment and decree of the appellate Court below. Therefore, he prays for dismissal of the appeal. However, after submissions of the learned Senior Counsel Mr. Alam regarding no objection about the decree for specific performance of contract in favour of the plaintiff. Mr. Mostafa Neaz Mohammad very candidly submits that he has no objection if the judgment is modified to that effect as per submission of the learned Advocate for the appellants. 

 14. Leave was granted to examine the submissions of the learned Senior Advocate for the appellants as to that having regard to the admitted fact that the land described in the "Bainanama" of the plaintiff and that of the decree these are not the same lands and having further regard to the fact that the High Court Division came to the finding that the suit land of Other Suit No. 61 of 1990 are not identical with the Other suit no. 54 of 1976 and there is no clash of interest between the defendant nos. 3-4 and the plaintiff with respect to the agreement Exhibit no. 4 (Bainanama). That the Single Judge committed an error of law in setting aside the judgment and decree of the Appellate court. That the High Court Division has committed an error of law in not holding that the plaintiff, by filing Other Suit No. 54 of 1976 (Other Suit No. 61 of 1990) for specific performance of contract, has not acquired any legal right in the suit land as such he is not entitled to get declaration that the judgment and decree passed in another suit between different parties being Other Suit No. 23 of 1977 in respect of the different suit land as illegal and void. 

 16. For obtaining a decree meant for specific performance of contract the plaintiff is required to prove the existence of a valid contract, execution of an agreement fairly and without any inducement, coercion or fraud and the question of limitation. 

 18. In view of the above the discussions the decision of the Appellant Court in dismissing the suit as a whole is found to be based upon total non application of judicial mind and not been supported by evidence. As such, it should be reversed and the judgment and order of the trial court as far as the judgments and decrees relate the relief of specific performance of contract. 

 19. On careful perusal of the schedules of the impugned Bainanama (exhibit no. 4) of the Other suit no. 61 of 1990 and Kabala nos. 7321 and 7322 of 1977 (exhibit no. Kha and Kha-1) of the other suit no. 23 of 1977 it was found that suit lands of the two cases are not identical. High Court Division too opine in the same line in its impugned judgment and order. Even so, High Court Division affirmed the trial court's decision declaring the registered Kabala nos. 7321 and 7322 of 1977 as void, illegal, without consideration in pursuance of its order of cancellation of judgment and decree of the other suit no. 23 of 1977. Consequently, our considered view is that High Court Division erred in law as well as fact on the face of the record resulting failure of justice in affirming the trial court's decision in toto. 

 20. Moreover, trial court reached in the decision of declaring the aforementioned two Kabalas as void, illegal, without consideration etc on the grounds and reasoning that the Kabalas were executed and registered on the same day of the compromise decree, as such, these were fraudulently executed and registered. However, without solid concrete basis it is not legally sustainable. The mere fact that the execution and registration of the Kabalas were taken at the same date can no way be deem as an, ingredient of conspiracy and swindle. In this context this Division's observations made in the case of Capital Tower Limited vs. Mirpur Mazar Co-operative Market Society Ltd. and others reported in 2005 25 BLD (AD) 91 that: 

 21. On the other hand, we cannot approve too the appellate courts observations that as a court of lower grade the learned Assistant Judge cannot cancel the judgment and decree of 02 grade senior court of a Joint District Judge. Trial court based its decision of cancellation of judgment and decree on findings of fraudulent practices and 'collusions. Because, it is an established rule of administration of justice that fraud vitiates everything. If fraud is established, then a court of the lowest tier can cancel even the judgment and order of the Apex court. It was held in the case of Government of Bangladesh and another vs. Mashiur Rahman and others [50 DLR(AD) 205] that: 

 "It is a cardinal principle of administration of justice that no result of any judicial proceeding should be allowed to receive judicial approval from any court of law whenever it is obtained by practicing fraud upon the court; reason being fraud demolishes the very foundation of sanctity of such judicial proceeding. It is also well established principle of law that fraud vitiates all judicial proceeding. Thus contravention of the provision of law, cannot be a valid ground for allowing an order obtained by fraud to stand. When the trial court itself on consideration of the materials on record was satisfied that a fraud had been committed in obtaining the ex parte decree it was the duty of the trial court to set aside the ex parte decree." 

 "It is true that fraud vitiates everything; even a judgment and decree affirmed by the apex Court of the country can be declared illegal and void by the trial Court if it is proved that the judgment and decree was obtained by practicing fraud upon Court." 

 23. The question is whether there was fraud in the execution and registration of the Kabala nos. 7321 and 7322 of 1977 and our answer from the above discussions is a negation. Hence, our considered view is that ordering portion of the trial court dated 27.02.1997 so far it relates the declaration of the registered Kabala nos. 7321 of 1977 and 7322 of 1977 as void, illegal, without consideration in pursuance of its order of cancellation of judgment and decree of the other suit no. 23 of 1977 be set aside. 

 24. On appreciation and sifting of evidences adduced trial court disbelieved the defendant's version of cases regarding their title and possession over the suit land and we observed that appellate court with-out discarding the findings based on strong evidences reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court. 

 26. Accordingly, this civil appeal is disposed of. The impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is modified. Other Suit No.54 of 1976 subsequently renumbered as Other Suit No.61 of 1990 so far as it relates to the decree for Specific Performance of Contract is allowed. The ordering portion of the trial Court dated 27.02.1997 so far as it relates to ২৩/৭৭ নং মোকদ্দমার রায় ডিক্রী এতদ্বারা বাতিল ক্রমে উক্ত ডিক্রী মূলে ৩/৪ নং বিবাদী বরাবর ১নং বিবাদী কর্তৃক সম্পাদিত ৭৩২১ এবং ৭৩২২ নং কবলা অবৈধ, বেআইনী পনশূন্য ঘোষনা করা হইল। This portion of the judgment is set aside.
